component_records.title: Program design, curriculum and credential architecture
component_records.description: Delivers the industry-informed online AI curriculum for Track A and Track B, built with an employer advisory group that reviews technical skills and learning milestones each cohort. The curriculum is structured as an immersive schedule that can run part-time or full-time, with defined skill-attainment assessments at each milestone and a stated credential (or explicit statement that none is issued) on completion. Curriculum development is completed or finalised in the mobilisation phase and refreshed each cohort against employer input, and the design documents the monthly timeline through first-cohort placement, training duration, cohort size and stipend level.

component_records.title: Outreach, recruitment and application/assessment process
component_records.description: Runs a targeted recruitment campaign for New Yorkers underrepresented in tech who cannot reasonably access training on their own, with channel plans for CUNY/SUNY campuses, community-based organisations and workforce partners. Delivers an online application and evaluation process with a documented low-income eligibility determination, a needs assessment that records each participant's barriers to success, and an individual success plan that routes supports accordingly. Recruitment targets are set to meet or exceed the 250-participant floor with a stretch plan above 400, and to keep low-income enrolment above 50%.

component_records.title: Training delivery, stipends and wrap-around supports
component_records.description: Delivers and manages the cohort-based training itself: instruction, cohort management, attendance and progress tracking, and professional development support throughout training. Each participant receives a stated stipend at the proposed level plus wrap-around supports — a mentor and a career coach with industry expertise, plus barrier-specific supports identified in the needs assessment. Delivery is staffed for both part-time and full-time schedules so participants with employment or caregiving obligations can complete the program.

component_records.title: Employer partnerships and placement engine
component_records.description: Cultivates and maintains relationships with leading New York tech employers to inform curriculum content and generate paid internship and full-time AI openings, supported by employer commitment letters submitted with the proposal. Runs a placement function that matches participants to paid internships (Track A) and full-time AI roles (Track B), prepares them for interviews, and tracks placements through to hire. Placement support is designed to meet the commitment that the majority of graduates secure paid internships or full-time employment in AI or a closely related field.

component_records.title: Performance data, reporting and ESD access
component_records.description: Implements a participant data system that captures every required data point — applicant, enrolment and completion counts with low-income percentages, paid internship and full-time placement rates with low-income percentages, participating colleges and employer partners — and makes the data available to ESD on request. Produces the progress reports and periodic meeting cadence that support ESD's performance assessment, and reports against the three annual performance metrics (participants served, low-income completion rate, placement rate) estimated in the proposal. The data model is built to absorb the additional data points ESD fixes during contract negotiation without re-platforming.

component_records.title: Budget, pricing and cost justification
component_records.description: Delivers a line-by-line budget per track, mapped to the 18-month program duration and capped at $2M per track, with personnel services broken out by job title, named staff, rate, fringe and percentage of time, and OTPS costs on separate lines. Budget lines cover staff salary and benefits, wraparound supports and the participant stipend level, and other program costs including curriculum development, marketing and events. Indirect costs are excluded entirely, and any cost match the bidder offers is indicated in the budget template to earn the additional scoring points.

component_records.title: Compliance, diversity and contract obligations
component_records.description: A dedicated compliance workstream carries the non-technical obligations of the contract: MWBE participation at the 30% goal and SDVOB participation at the 6% goal, with OCSD-4 Utilization Plans, good faith effort documentation, quarterly Workforce Utilization Reports and monthly SDVOB compliance reporting; insurance placement at the required limits with ESD named additional insured and waiver of subrogation; lobbying-law and ethics compliance including the restricted-period contact rules and periodic 139-j/139-k updates; vendor responsibility registration and ongoing responsibility; and acceptance of Schedule A, OSC approval and change-order procedures. Also covers the bidder's entity eligibility, lead-entity designation for any team, and the domain experience evidence required to qualify. The same workstream runs the bid calendar: it logs every clarification the bid team raises, consolidates them into a single written submission to the designated contacts at AI.Prep@esd.ny.gov, and files them ahead of the August 29, 2025 question deadline so the answers due September 12, 2025 can still shape the proposal.

component_records.title: Mobilisation, project management and staffing continuity
component_records.description: Runs a mobilisation phase from the anticipated 1 January 2026 start to first-cohort launch, covering curriculum finalisation, employer commitment conversion, systems set-up, compliance filings and staff onboarding for ESD approval. Provides day-to-day program management with a named core team, monthly timeline tracking through first-cohort placement, and a staff continuity plan that notifies ESD immediately of any proposed change and offers the substitute's experience and an interview before approval. Manages any subcontractors disclosed in the proposal and keeps all staff qualified and legally entitled to work in New York.

pairs.requirement_text: The contractor must develop the curriculum for and administer the AI Prep program for Track A (AI Prep 4 Internships) and/or Track B (AI Prep 4 Jobs).
Track A (AI Prep 4 Internships) must provide low-income matriculating undergraduate students with AI training aimed at securing paid internship opportunities at leading tech companies.

Track B (AI Prep 4 Jobs) must connect low-income New Yorkers with barriers to employment to AI jobs through an accelerated training or bootcamp that serves as an alternative to traditional degree programs.
The administrator must develop and deliver a comprehensive AI technology training program for low-income college students that includes paid internship placements.
The administrator must design an industry-informed AI curriculum.
The program must consist of online courses in AI whose curriculum incorporates industry input regarding technical skills and learning milestones.
The program must include a training schedule that is immersive and can be delivered part-time or full-time.
The program must include evaluation metrics to measure participant skill attainment during training.
The program must state the credentials expected as a result of training completion, if applicable.

The bidder must decide whether to accept unknown terms and file written concerns with its Administrative Proposal, while the RFP simultaneously forbids including Schedule A information in the submission. If Schedule A contains unacceptable liability, indemnity or data-ownership terms, the bidder either walks away after award or absorbs unplanned legal and insurance cost. items.text: MWBE 30% and SDVOB 6% goals carry liquidated damages and payment withholding. The contract sets a 30% MWBE and 6% SDVOB participation goal, with good faith effort documentation, quarterly Workforce Utilization Reports and monthly SDVOB compliance reporting. Failure to meet the goals can trigger liquidated damages equal to the shortfall and withholding of payment, and the RFP does not settle whether the goals apply to total contract value or subcontracting spend or whether good faith efforts alone suffice. The damages and withholding provisions are explicit (R191, R195, R196, R250), but the base against which the goals are measured and the waiver standard are left open, so exposure depends on facts the RFP does not settle.

The RFP requires a stipend line in the budget and a stated stipend level in the Project Plan but gives no rate, duration or expected share of the award. Stipends are mandatory (R016, R051, R084) and the cap is fixed (R034), but the RFP leaves the rate and allocation open, so the budget model turns on an unsettled fact.
